**Summary:**
The global food system faces mounting pressures as the world population is projected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050, requiring a 60% increase in food production while climate change, water scarcity, and soil degradation already threaten agricultural output—33% of arable land has reduced productivity, and the Ogallala Aquifer is being depleted faster than it recharges. Agriculture contributes roughly 25% of greenhouse gas emissions through deforestation, livestock, and fertilizers, while approximately one-third of all food produced is lost or wasted. Various technological and agricultural innovations such as precision agriculture, vertical farming, alternative proteins, drought-resistant crops, and regenerative farming practices offer potential solutions, though policy changes around subsidies, trade, and carbon pricing will also be needed. The core challenge remains scaling these solutions while ensuring food remains affordable and accessible to the world's poorest populations.
